text:
rafael: Heads up — came across a weird localserve auth failure on macOS. Fresh install via the standalone pkg and localserve couldn't find my token when using the sample app. Login reported success though.

jen: which macOS version and install method? Homebrew vs pkg tends to put things in different prefixes.

rafael: macOS 13.7, Apple Silicon. I used the downloadable .pkg from releases (not homebrew). `redwoodctl auth login` printed success. Starting the sample app with `redwoodctl localserve --profile=work` yields 401s.

mira: can you show `redwoodctl config get profiles.path` and `ls ~/Library/Preferences` or `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME`? We've got an older change where the CLI respects XDG on unix-y platforms but the pkg installer was still writing into Library/Application Support.

rafael: sure:
```
$ redwoodctl config get profiles.path
/Users/rafael/.config/redwoodctl/profiles

$ echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME

# (blank)

$ ls ~/Library/Application\ Support/Redwood/profiles
default/token.json
```

ops: there it is — pkg wrote to ~/Library/Application Support/Redwood but the CLI default is ~/.config/redwoodctl. Homebrew installs put things in ~/.config usually. That mismatch could happen when we changed to XDG earlier.

jen: ideally the installer should detect XDG_CONFIG_HOME and write there, or the CLI should fallback to Library/Application Support for pkg installs. Which direction do we prefer?

mira: UX-wise, respect XDG if set; otherwise, on mac we should keep backward compatibility with Library/Application Support until installers are aligned. It's basically an onboarding friction: people run login from an installer-launched flow and then `localserve` or sample apps fail.

rafael: workaround that worked for me: `redwoodctl config set profiles.path "/Users/rafael/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles"` and restart shell. Also `export REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles"` would work for a temporary fix.

qa-bot: Filing ticket: CM-621 - "macOS pkg installer writes profiles to Library/Application Support while CLI defaults to XDG ~/.config; cause onboarding break for sample apps". Assigned to eng-packaging.

ops: QA checklist on the ticket: verify fresh pkg install, homebrew install, and upgrade path. Ensure we don't duplicate or overwrite profiles when migrating. Also test for users who have XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to a custom path.

mira: small edge we noticed in CI/WSL combos: in some WSL2 CI images the headless login flow uses the OS-specific opener command (open on mac, xdg-open on linux, start on windows) even when running in non-GUI contexts. That results in a noisy error like "failed to open browser". For headless and --no-browser flags, the CLI should never attempt to spawn an opener.

jen: filed CM-622 for that: "redwoodctl auth login --headless/CI must not spawn platform opener if DISPLAY unset or in non-interactive sessions". Suggested fix: detect isatty and XDG_SESSION_TYPE or DISPLAY on linux, and skip spawn.

rafael: also discovered token shape differences between old token.json and new XDG path after a partial migration: older token.json had `expires_at` while new CLI expects `expiry`. During a manual migration I had to rename the field or localserve failed to parse. We should accept both keys for a deprecation window.

ops: good catch — adding to CM-621: compatibility shim to accept `expires_at` or `expiry` and convert at load time, and a migration tool `redwoodctl profiles migrate --from=legacy` to safely move files with checksums.

mira: for release notes, we should include both the env var REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR and `redwoodctl config set profiles.path` examples, and a one-liner migrate script suggestion. Eg:
```
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles"
cp -R "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles/"* "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/"
```
Also mention the CLI will auto-detect both locations for the next two releases.

jen: scheduling packaging fix. I'll coordinate with infra to publish a patch pkg and a homebrew cask update. Can someone from QA validate the migration steps on both Intel and Apple Silicon images?

rafael: I'll run through Intel/Silicon and WSL/CI sim in my fork and report back. Thanks for the quick triage.

ops: infra-bot: canary publish requested: packaging/macos-profile-xdg-fix -> canary macos at 2026-03-02T09:00Z

mira: thanks — if QA re-tests sample-app-onboarding flows that cover `redwoodctl init`, `auth login`, and `localserve` that would be ideal. I'll add a sample-app checklist to docs. :memo:
